subject: Fill colours that look good in b/w

messages.author: f5db6210b85ed606
messages.subject: Fill colours that look good in b/w
parts:
Hi everybody,
I love the plots that ggplot2 churn out and I like the "grammar" which
I am slowly getting into.
However, even though I like the default settings, when I print this
graph:

qplot(x,y ,data = subset(mydata, !is.na(x)),
geom = "boxplot", fill = factor(a)) + theme_bw()

where the fill colour is determined by a 2-level factor, the default
colours ("reddish" and "greenish") are indistinguishable on a b/w
printout.
I have been trying to find info on how to set the two colours manually
(e.g. I want grey and white fill colour) but I can't seem to find it
anywhere.
Any tips would be appreciated on how to achieve this

regards

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: Fill colours that look good in b/w
parts:
The default color scale yields indistinguishable greyscale tones by
intent. This ensures that the full color versions of the graphics
avoid confounding hue with brightness.

To manually specify the colours used in the colour scale, see
?scale_colour_manual

messages.author: f5db6210b85ed606
messages.subject: Re: Fill colours that look good in b/w
parts:
scale_fill_grey() was the one - however default settings (black fill
and white fill)
was not my liking (black makes it hard to see the median line unless I
use white lines...)
With a little bit of tweaking and scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey",
"white")) it came right.
Thanks everybody!

J
